From Cold Food Storage Chart (FoodSafety.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services), 2023):
- Egg salad stored in the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below can be kept for 3 to 4 days. [4]

From Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- Ground meats should be cooked to an internal temperature of 160 °F (71.1 °C). [2]

From Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- In the refrigerator, a frozen turkey requires approximately 24 hours for every 4 to 5 pounds. [1]

From Five Keys to Safer Food Manual (World Health Organization, 2006):
- The five keys to safer food are: keep clean; separate raw and cooked; cook thoroughly; keep food at safe temperatures; and use safe water and raw materials. [1]

These documents each address this:

How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely (Food Standards Agency, 2017):
- Defrost food in the fridge using a container large enough to catch drips and use it within 24 hours after fully thawed. [1]
- If a fridge container is not possible, defrost using a microwave on the defrost setting directly before cooking. [1]
- Always clean surfaces, chopping boards, utensils, plates and hands with warm soapy water after they have touched raw or thawing meat. [1]

Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- In the refrigerator is the safest way to thaw meat and poultry, placing the food on a plate or in a pan to catch any juices. [4]
- For faster thawing, submerge a sealed package in cold water, changing the water every 30 minutes, and cook immediately after thawing. [4]
- When using a microwave to thaw, follow the manufacturer’s instructions and cook the food immediately after thawing. [4]

From What are healthy diets? Joint statement by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the World Health Organization (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Health Organization, 2024):
- A healthy diet provides enough essential nutrients to prevent deficiencies and promote health without excess. [1]
- A healthy diet includes appropriate energy intake and sources of fats, carbohydrates and proteins to promote healthy weight, growth and disease prevention. [1]
- A healthy diet limits consumption of foods, nutrients or other compounds associated with detrimental health effects. [1]
- A healthy diet includes a wide variety of nutritious foods within and across food groups to favour nutrient adequacy and health‑promoting substances. [1]
- A healthy diet requires that foods and beverages are safe and will not cause adverse health effects when prepared or eaten. [1]

From The Eatwell Guide (Public Health England, 2018):
- Adults should aim to drink 6-8 glasses of fluid each day. [1]

From Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- Raw chicken should not be rinsed before cooking. [1]

These documents each address this:

The Eatwell Guide (Public Health England, 2018):
- Unsaturated oils such as vegetable, rapeseed and olive oil are healthier and should replace saturated fats to help reduce blood cholesterol. [1]
- Choosing lower‑fat spreads instead of butter is recommended to reduce saturated fat intake. [1]
- All types of fat are high in energy and should be limited in the diet. [1]
- Use oils and soft spreads made from unsaturated oils sparingly because they are high in fat and calories. [5]
- Select oils that are high in unsaturated fat and low in saturated fat, and choose lower‑fat spreads when possible. [5]

What are healthy diets? Joint statement by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the World Health Organization (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Health Organization, 2024):
- Adults should limit total fat intake to 30% of total energy intake or less. [3]
- Adults and children should reduce saturated fatty acid intake to 10% of total energy intake. [3]
- Adults should obtain 6–10% of total energy intake from polyunsaturated fats, with the remainder of fat intake coming from monounsaturated fats from plant sources. [4]

These documents each address this:

How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely (Food Standards Agency, 2017):
- The fridge should be set between 0 °C and 5 °C. [3]
- The fridge should be set between 0 °C and 5 °C. [4]

Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- Cold food should be kept at 40 °F (4.44 °C) or below. [5]

Cold Food Storage Chart (FoodSafety.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services), 2023):
- Cooked leftovers such as meat or poultry can be stored in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days. [6]
- Leftover pizza can be stored in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days. [6]

These documents each address this:

The Eatwell Guide (Public Health England, 2018):
- The Eatwell Guide states that ideally no more than 5% of energy should come from free sugars. [1]
- For children aged 4‑6 years, the Eatwell Guide recommends no more than 19 g of free sugars per day. [1]
- For children aged 7‑10 years, the Eatwell Guide recommends no more than 24 g of free sugars per day. [1]
- For people aged 11 years and older, the Eatwell Guide recommends no more than 30 g of free sugars per day. [1]

Healthy diet (Fact sheet N°394) (World Health Organization, 2018):
- The WHO fact sheet advises that free sugars intake should be reduced to less than 10% of total energy intake. [2]
- The WHO fact sheet notes that reducing free sugars intake to less than 5% of total energy provides additional health benefits. [2]
- The WHO fact sheet states that consuming free sugars increases the risk of dental caries. [2]
- The WHO fact sheet recommends limiting foods and drinks high in sugars, such as sugary snacks, candies and sugar‑sweetened beverages. [2]

These documents each address this:

Healthy diet (Fact sheet N°394) (World Health Organization, 2018):
- Reducing salt intake to the recommended level of less than 5 g per day could prevent 1.7 million deaths each year. [1]

What are healthy diets? Joint statement by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the World Health Organization (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Health Organization, 2024):
- WHO recommends a reduction to <2 g/day sodium (5 g/day salt) in adults. [3]
- Sodium intake should be restricted to 2 grams per day (corresponding to 5 grams of table salt) in adults. [5]

The Eatwell Guide (Public Health England, 2018):
- Adults should eat no more than 6 g of salt a day. [4]

These documents each address this:

Kitchen Companion: Your Safe Food Handbook (U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, 2015):
- Keep hot food at 140 °F (60 °C) or above. [2]
- Keep cold food at 40 °F (4.44 °C) or below. [2]

How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely (Food Standards Agency, 2017):
- Set the refrigerator temperature between 0 °C and 5 °C. [3]
- Set the freezer temperature around –18 °C. [4]
- Do not place hot or warm food directly into the refrigerator; cool it at room temperature and refrigerate within one to two hours. [3]
- Store leftovers in the refrigerator and eat them within 48 hours. [3]
- Eat leftovers within two days or freeze them if longer storage is needed. [4]
- Keep chilled food out of the fridge for no more than four hours during preparation. [3]

- Use the microwave’s defrost setting directly before cooking if you cannot defrost in the fridge. [1]
- Use the meat within 24 hours after it has been fully defrosted. [1]

From The Eatwell Guide (Public Health England, 2018):
